properties.decision:
Recorded as BRAINSTORMING, not as a proposal. dev_storyflow agent, 2026-09-06 on 0.48.0, wish #35, in their words: "the 'engine validates no edge' capability was measured before building and turned out already true one layer down (the storage engine validates every edge) — the design's claim was wrong, not the code. reflow2 held the wrong claim in the capability's description; `prose_currency` surfaced it when the status moved and I rewrote it. Small wish: when a capability is set `verified` with NO change event linked since it was `planned`, say so — that is exactly the 'already true' case and it deserves a nudge to explain why nothing was built."

THE SHAPE: the same family as prose_currency (cap:a-status-advance-says-whether-its-prose-predates-it) — a note in the reply that moved the status, silent unless the condition holds, never a judgement. The condition is computable: the capability's incoming CHANGED edges, and those of the artifacts that REALIZE it, all predate the last status move or are absent.

OPTIONS: (a) a `no_change_since_planned` block on set_capability_status when the status moves to realized/verified and no dated ChangeEvent touched the capability or its realizers since it left `planned` — quoting the description and asking whether the claim was already true or the change simply went unrecorded. (b) fold it into prose_currency as a second sentence. (c) a detector instead of a reply note (a verified capability with no realizing artifact changed since planned) — but that is close to `unrealized_capability` and to the overtaken-defect detector's undated-change blindness: half of this design's own ChangeEvents carry no date, so 'nothing changed since' is often 'nothing DATED changed since'.
properties.name: OPEN — when a capability is set `verified` with NO ChangeEvent touching it (or a realizing artifact) since it was `planned`, should the reply say so — the "it was already true" case that deserves an explanation of why nothing was built?
properties.rationale: COUNTER-ARGUMENTS. Two honest readings of the condition — 'it was already true' and 'the change went unrecorded' — and the note cannot tell them apart, so it must ask rather than conclude (dec:report-dont-judge). Undated ChangeEvents make the computation lie in the unrecorded direction; the note should count them and say so, as the overtaken-defect detector does. (b) keeps one block per status move, which is kinder to the reader than two. A RANKING IS A FINDING: (a)/(b) are cheap and the same shape as a check the field has now confirmed three times in one day (fact:prose-currency-caught-three-stale-descriptions-in-one-field-session); (c) is a nag. Anthony's call.
